Hey Guys

We are currently evaluating using shinyapps.io for deploying some of our production apps (bioinformatics based). For our implementation we have few requirements.

1. we need to be able to connect to our server to fetch data in real time. This means we need to be able to store username/passwd information
2. download data from our server to shinyapps server
3. install R/Python libs for code dependencies

Just wondering if RStudio folks or community have addressed similar issues before.

Best,
-Abhi

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] evaluating shinyapps.io - bioinformatics data heavy apps
parts:
Hi,

See my responses inline.

On Tue, Jun 30, 2015 at 2:36 PM, Abhishek Pratap <abhish...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hey Guys

We are currently evaluating using shinyapps.io for deploying some of our production apps (bioinformatics based). For our implementation we have few requirements.

1. we need to be able to connect to our server to fetch data in real time. This means we need to be able to store username/passwd information
Sure. Many people like to store their username / passwords in a .Rprofile which is included in the app when deploying.
2. download data from our server to shinyapps server

Obviously this is dependent on how you are downloaded the data, but as long as the shinyapps.io servers have access this should be fine. Keep in mind however, that data downloaded will not be saved after re-deploying the application (all data written to a shinyapps.io application instance is ephemeral). So downloaded large amounts of data may result in performance issues. Read more here.
3. install R/Python libs for code dependencies

This may be an issue. Installing most R packages is supported, and even custom packages hosted on GitHub. However python packages may not be supported. shinyapps.io doesn't currently support installing arbitrary python packages at this time. This is something we've discussed adding, but have no immediate plans at thsi time. It may be possible to port your python code to R.

Just wondering if RStudio folks or community have addressed similar issues before.

Best,
-Abhi
